desc: Khardung La is a high mountain pass in the Ladakh region of India, located on the Ladakh Range north of Leh. At an elevation of 5,359 meters, it is one of the highest motorable passes in the world. The pass connects Leh to the Shyok and Nubra valleys and was historically an important trade route to Central Asia. The pass was built in 1976 by the Border Roads Organisation for military logistics. It serves as the primary access route to the Siachen Glacier military posts. The pass features a small temple and offers stunning views of the Karakoram Range. Temperatures at the pass can drop to -40°C in winter.
fact: Khardung La is one of the highest motorable passes in the world at 5,359 meters · It connects Leh to the Shyok and Nubra valleys in Ladakh · It was built in 1976 by the Border Roads Organisation for military access to Siachen · Temperatures can drop to -40°C in winter

desc: The Khyber Pass is a mountain pass in the Spin Ghar range connecting Pakistan and Afghanistan, at an elevation of 1,070 meters. It is one of the most historically significant mountain passes in the world, serving as a strategic trade and invasion route between Central Asia and the Indian subcontinent for over 3,000 years. Conquerors including Alexander the Great, Mahmud of Ghazni, Babur, and Nadir Shah used the pass to invade India. The pass is about 53 km long, winding through rugged terrain with steep walls. The Khyber Railway and the modern Karakoram Highway traverse the pass. The pass is controlled by Pakistan and is part of the historic Silk Road network.
fact: The Khyber Pass is one of the most historically significant passes, connecting Pakistan and Afghanistan · It was used by Alexander the Great, Mahmud of Ghazni, Babur, and Nadir Shah to invade India · The pass is 53 km long at 1,070 meters elevation in the Spin Ghar range · It has been a strategic trade and invasion route for over 3,000 years

desc: The Stelvio Pass is the highest paved mountain pass in the Eastern Alps at 2,757 meters, located in the Italian Alps near the Swiss border. The pass road, built between 1820 and 1825 by the Austrian Empire, features 48 hairpin turns on the northern side, making it one of the most spectacular driving routes in the world. The pass connects the Valtellina valley with the Adige valley and the town of Bormio. It is a legendary destination for cyclists, frequently featured in the Giro d'Italia cycling race. The pass is surrounded by the Stelvio National Park, the largest protected area in the Alps, with glaciers, alpine meadows, and wildlife including ibex and chamois.
fact: The Stelvio Pass is the highest paved pass in the Eastern Alps at 2,757 meters · The pass road features 48 hairpin turns, built by the Austrian Empire 1820-1825 · It is a legendary cycling destination featured in the Giro d'Italia · The pass is surrounded by Stelvio National Park, the largest Alpine protected area

desc: Rohtang Pass is a high mountain pass in the Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas, located in Himachal Pradesh at an elevation of 3,978 meters. It connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti valleys and provides access to Leh. The name 'Rohtang' means 'pile of corpses' in the local language, referring to the many travelers who died attempting to cross the pass. The pass is open from May to November and is a major tourist attraction from Manali. It offers panoramic views of the surrounding peaks and glaciers. The Atal Tunnel, the longest highway tunnel in the world at 9.02 km, was completed in 2020 to bypass the pass and provide year-round connectivity.
fact: Rohtang Pass is at 3,978 meters in the Pir Panjal range, connecting Kullu Valley to Lahaul and Spiti · The name means 'pile of corpses' from the many travelers who died crossing it · The 9.02 km Atal Tunnel, the world's longest highway tunnel, bypasses the pass · It is a major tourist attraction from Manali, open May to November

desc: Chang La is a high mountain pass in the Ladakh region of India, located on the way to Pangong Tso lake. At an elevation of 5,360 meters, it is the third-highest motorable pass in the world. The pass road connects Leh with the Changthang region and the China border. The area is home to the Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary and the unique Changthangi pashmina goat. The pass is surrounded by stark, high-altitude desert landscapes. The Chang La is known for being the highest pass patrolled by the Border Roads Organisation and features a small temple dedicated to a local deity. Temperatures at the pass regularly drop below -30°C in winter.
fact: Chang La is the third-highest motorable pass in the world at 5,360 meters in Ladakh · It connects Leh to Pangong Tso lake and the Changthang region · It is home to the Changthangi pashmina goat and high-altitude desert landscape · The pass features a small temple and is patrolled by the Border Roads Organisation
